text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details. Since you mentioned sunbathing, have these lesions appeared after prolonged exposure to the sun, and are they itchy or painful?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis. These findings are consistent with actinic keratosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis. Given your history of sun exposure and the biopsy confirming atypical keratinocytes, I recommend a follow-up in three months to monitor for any transformation into squamous cell carcinoma, or we can discuss cryotherapy now if the lesion is symptomatic.
